evals.prompt:
Build a paper-evaluation pack in the folder I name. Derive every criterion only from these two SYNTHETIC papers (invented for this test; not real publications). Do not retrieve the web. Do not save PDFs. Do not git commit. Python standard library only.

Paper PLAN: evals/files/SYNTHETIC_paper_plan.txt — a research PLAN with no results. Gaps: no QA guidelines, unclear quality-task processes, insufficient performance-reporting standards for model comparison. Planned methods: literature study, expert validation, pilot with two teams. Treat it as a proposal. Never call its framework validated.

Paper CASE: evals/files/SYNTHETIC_paper_casestudy.txt — a completed case study. Feasibility and acceptance are separate questions. Desk-checking is a checklist-guided self-review, not a structured inspection. Variability modeling was feasible but needed a different language to cover important variants. Developers accepted both parts. The study reports that limit.

Output folder: the eval outputs directory you were given. Reviewer label: ai-draft. Include README, source-trace.md, rubric.csv, desk-check-checklist.md, templates/evaluation-template.md, scores/scores.csv, scripts/score_papers.py (standard library), scripts/tests with a SYNTHETIC fixture, and AI_INTERACTION_LOG.md. Tag each criterion full-text, abstract-only, or adapted. Score both SYNTHETIC papers as ai-draft, run the scorer and tests, and report totals. Do not invent a second reviewer.
evals.expected_output: A pack whose criteria trace to the two SYNTHETIC abstracts, with support levels, a plan not described as validated, a passing scorer run, and no second-reviewer scores.
assertions: Output folder contains rubric.csv with the required header columns including support_level
Every rubric support_level is full-text, abstract-only, or adapted
The pack does not describe the PLAN paper's framework as validated
No PDF file is written in the output folder
scores.csv reviewer values are only ai-draft
The scorer or its report is present (summary.csv or a VALIDATION PASSED log)
At least one criterion traces to performance reporting or model comparison
At least one criterion traces to feasibility and acceptance as separate questions

evals.prompt:
I already have a SYNTHETIC paper-evaluation pack (invented data, not real papers). Run the bundled scorer and report per-paper totals and Cohen's kappa. Do not invent a third reviewer. Do not install packages. Do not git commit.

Use the skill's scripts/score_papers.py. Rubric and two-reviewer scores are the SYNTHETIC fixtures that the skill's tests use, or recreate the same columns: criterion_id, rubric_version, criterion, guiding_question, score_0_anchor, score_1_anchor, score_2_anchor, source_paper, source_location, support_level for the rubric; paper_id, doi, reviewer, rubric_version, criterion_id, score, evidence_location, note for scores.

If the skill ships scripts/tests/fixtures/SYNTHETIC_*.csv, run those. Otherwise create a tiny two-reviewer fixture, run python -B scripts/score_papers.py with explicit --rubric --scores --summary paths in the eval outputs folder, and print the report. A failing script is a failed result.
evals.expected_output: VALIDATION PASSED, per-paper totals, and kappa rows for the reviewer pair. No fabricated extra reviewer.
assertions: Stdout or a saved report contains VALIDATION PASSED
The report includes Cohen's kappa for a reviewer pair
If the shipped two-reviewer fixture was used, S01 kappa is 1.0000 and S02 kappa is 0.6364
No reviewer other than syn-rev1 and syn-rev2 is introduced
summary.csv is written to the eval outputs folder
